newsitem.title: USA: Statoil to take stake in Texaco's Fuji.
newsitem.headline: Statoil to take stake in Texaco's Fuji.

text.p: Texaco said Thursday Statoil Exploration (US) Inc. will become a 35 percent working interest partner in Texaco's Fuji project in the deepwater Gulf of Mexico.

Fuji, presently 100 percent owned by Texaco Exploration and Production Inc, is comprised of six Green Canyon lease blocks in the Gulf of Mexico. The discovery well, drilled on Green Canyong Block 506, was one of three previously announced Texaco-operated discoveries in the deepwater Gulf of Mexico. The other two are Petronius (Viosca Knoll 786) and Gemini (Mississippi Canyon 292).

The agreement calls for Den Norske Stats Oljeselskap A/S U.S. unit's participation in an initial delineation well at Green Canyon Block 505 in exchange for earning a Statoil 35 percent interest in the discovery well.
Terms of the transaction were not disclosed, Texaco said.
Spokesman Pierre DeGruy declined to elaborate, but did note the term "farm in" was not used in any of the discussions on the agreement.
Texaco said Statoil will also have the option of becoming a 35 percent interest holder in the balance of the leases comprising the Fuji project.

The Green Canyon Block 506 wildcat, located 175 miles (280 kilometers) southwest of New Orleans in 4,243 feet (1,293 meters) of water, was drilled to a total depth of 21,200 feet (6,462 meters) and temporarily plugged and abandoned in February 1995. The discovery established significant hydrocarbons in the exploratory trend, and has reduced risk for several surrounding, high impact prospects.
